issues.description: The template Stock class defines findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) but elsewhere (both within the template and in the problem specification and solution) the expected signature is findStockIngredient(String). Specifically, Stock.add and Stock.take in the template call findStockIngredient with a single String argument, and the UML in the problem statement and the solution implementation use a single-parameter method. This mismatch will cause compilation errors in the template and confuses students about the correct method signature to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template Stock.findStockIngredient signature with the problem statement and solution by changing it to findStockIngredient(String name). Update its implementation accordingly. Ensure all internal calls (add, take, etc.) use the single-parameter method. Alternatively, if a caseSensitive parameter is required, update all usages and the problem statement/UML to reflect the two-parameter signature consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (orders and stock) in the constructor, but it also explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and final (shared across instances). Initializing a static final stock in an instance constructor is contradictory and may confuse students about where and how to initialize the static final field. The solution initializes the static final stock at declaration instead.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement: state that the static final stock should be initialized at its declaration (or in a static initializer) rather than in the instance constructor. Update the text that currently instructs initializing 'in the constructor of SealSaloon' to avoid suggesting instance-construction of a static final field.

issues.description: The Stock.findStockIngredient method is referenced with a single String parameter in the problem statement and the solution, but the template implementation declares findStockIngredient(String, boolean). This mismatched signature (extra boolean parameter in the template) breaks the direct mapping from the problem description to the starter code and to the expected solution API, likely confusing students about which method to use and causing compilation/usage mismatch when following the exercise instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the problem statement and solution by providing a single-parameter method: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Either rename the existing template method to the single-argument signature or add an overload findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the two-argument method with the desired default case-sensitivity. This will align template, problem statement, and solution names and avoid student confusion.
